description: NPC dossier background: where a person came from, what they used to do, one event that shaped them and a talent. Origin text is a participle phrase used as 'I was <text>.'; goblinoid entries carry speakers=[goblinoid]. Original prose; generic heroic fantasy.

entries.text: raised on a river barge that never stayed anywhere long
born in a lighthouse keeper's cottage on a windy headland
fostered by a travelling puppet troupe
brought up in a mill town where everyone knew everyone's business
raised in a shepherd's hut high above the snowline
born below stairs in a noble house, underfoot in a great kitchen
left at a shrine gate as an infant and raised by its keepers
raised under a market stall, learning to haggle before learning to read
born in a fen village where the roads are boats
grown up in a trade caravan, never sleeping twice in the same bed
raised in a quarry camp where the quiet was the strange part
raised on a ruined estate, in the last household left standing
grown up on the salt flats, boiling brine with the whole family
brought up in a house of copyists, with ink on every finger
born in a crowded warren beneath an old mill
raised in a hill-cave clan that moved with every season
brought up in the crumbling lower floors of a ruined watchtower
born in the old drain tunnels beneath a town, learning every way out
raised in a squatters' camp under a stone bridge
born in an abandoned mine, where every echo was a friend or a foe
a ship's cook
entries.speak: I fed a ship's crew for six years. A galley hears everything, and I heard plenty.

entries.text: a mule driver on the high roads
entries.speak: I drove mules over the high roads. You learn which stretches are safe and which only look it.

entries.text: an apprentice bell-founder
entries.speak: I spent four years pouring bronze for bells. I can still hear a flat note across a street.

entries.text: a courier for a grain merchant
entries.speak: I carried letters for a grain merchant. I know most of the lanes between the towns around here.

entries.text: a journeyman tailor
entries.speak: I stitched coats for a living. I can tell a person's trade from how their sleeves wear.

entries.text: a quartermaster's clerk
entries.speak: I counted boots and bread for an army that has since gone home. Count anything long enough and you learn who is fibbing.

entries.text: a rope-walker with a travelling fair
entries.speak: I walked ropes with a travelling fair until my knee told me to stop.

entries.text: a beekeeper's hand
entries.speak: I kept bees. Patience, smoke and no sudden movements. It works on people too.

entries.text: a copyist in a counting house
entries.speak: I copied ledgers for a counting house. Numbers lie less than people do, though not by much.

entries.text: a ferry hand on the wide river
entries.speak: I poled a ferry for years. A river teaches you to wait and to watch.

entries.text: a stonemason's apprentice
entries.speak: I cut stone for a hall I never saw finished. I still look at walls to see who built them.

entries.text: a lamplighter
entries.speak: I lit the lamps of a whole district every dusk. Nobody looks at the lamplighter, so I saw a great deal.

entries.text: a net-mender on the harbor
entries.speak: I mended nets on the harbor. You learn to tell a clean tear from a cut.

entries.text: a healer's aide
entries.speak: I carried bandages for a healer through a fever year. Little frightens me now.

entries.text: a street singer
entries.speak: I sang for coins on street corners. A crowd will tell you what it thinks without saying a word.

entries.text: a stable hand at a coaching inn
entries.speak: I mucked out a coaching inn for years. Every traveller leaves a story with the horse.

entries.text: a scavenger of the town middens
entries.speak: I picked through the town's leavings for years. You would be amazed what people throw away.

entries.text: a lookout for a larger band
entries.speak: I watched roads for a bigger band. Sit still long enough and the whole world walks past.

entries.text: a tunnel digger
entries.speak: I dug tunnels. I can tell you the sound of a floor that is about to give way.

entries.text: a collector of bright things for the chief
entries.speak: I collected shiny things for the chief. I can spot a coin across a crowded room.

entries.text: survived the spring flood that took the family home
entries.speak: The spring flood took our house when I was nine. We rebuilt higher up, and I have never trusted a calm river since.

entries.text: was apprenticed away at twelve to a stern master
entries.speak: They sent me off at twelve to a master who taught everything but kindness. I learned the rest myself.

entries.text: found a purse of silver as a child and returned it
entries.speak: I found a purse of silver on a road when I was small and carried it all the way back to its owner. Their thanks set the course of my life.

entries.text: lived through a fever winter that emptied half the street
entries.speak: There was a fever winter when half our street was lost. I learned that year who comes to the door and who does not.

entries.text: lost a parent young and was raised by the neighbours
entries.speak: My mother was gone before I was ten, and the whole street raised me after. I owe every one of them.

entries.text: walked alone to a distant city at fifteen
entries.speak: I walked alone to the nearest great city at fifteen. It took eleven days and one very lucky ride on a hay cart.

entries.text: won a harvest footrace and was told it would lead somewhere
entries.speak: I won the harvest footrace one autumn and was told it would lead somewhere. It led here, which is not nowhere.

entries.text: helped save the records when the guildhall burned
entries.speak: I helped carry the records out when the guildhall burned. I smelled smoke in my sleep for a year.

entries.text: was sheltered by a stranger during a storm
entries.speak: A stranger took me in once, during a storm, and asked for nothing. I have been trying to repay it ever since.

entries.text: watched an argument end a forty-year friendship
entries.speak: I watched two old friends part over a trivial thing after forty years. I decided never to let a small quarrel grow.

entries.text: learned to read from a widow who asked only that they teach another
entries.speak: A widow taught me my letters and asked only that I teach someone else. I have kept to that bargain.

entries.text: was caught at the edge of a border skirmish and walked away unharmed
entries.speak: I was caught at the edge of a border skirmish once and walked away without a scratch. I do not take that for granted.

entries.text: walked a long pilgrim road and came home changed
entries.speak: I walked a long pilgrim road when I was young. I came home quieter and, I hope, kinder.

entries.text: stood watch the night every bell in town rang unaccountably
entries.speak: I stood watch the night every bell in town rang for no reason anyone could find. We never did learn why.

entries.text: once cooked a feast for a hundred from almost nothing
entries.speak: I once cooked a feast for a hundred people from nearly nothing. I have been proud of it for twenty years.

entries.text: was driven from a warren in a lean winter and found a new band
entries.speak: A lean winter drove me out of my first warren. I found a new band, and I have not gone hungry since, mostly.

entries.text: carried off a whole farmhouse supper and was celebrated for a month
entries.speak: I once carried off a whole farmhouse supper. They sang about it for a month, and the farmers did not.

entries.text: was left behind in a hasty move and walked three days to catch up
entries.speak: They left me behind in a hasty move once. I walked three days to catch up, and I have never let anyone forget it.

entries.text: lost a tooth in a famous brawl and tells it differently every time
entries.speak: I lost a tooth in a famous brawl. The story gets better every time I tell it.

entries.text: built a first trap that caught nothing but the chief's hat
entries.speak: The first trap I ever built caught nothing but the chief's hat. I was not popular that week.

entries.text: can tell a lie from a mistake by watching the hands
remembers every face and what it was wearing
can imitate any bird call
never forgets a debt, owed or owing
can mend almost anything with twine and patience
keeps a straight face through anything
sings well enough to hush a room
reads the weather in the smell of the air
knows every lane within a day's walk
puts strangers at ease within a minute
counts anything at a glance
sleeps anywhere, instantly
